title: Improve dedicated autoscaler: burst smoothing and per-pool utilization reporting (v33)
author: Liam Chen
description: Context: Customers operating Dedicated fleets observed unstable short-term scale-ups during bursty traffic. The existing token-bucket based burst allowance accrual produced spikes in 'scale_needed' signals when transient queueing events briefly increased demand, which caused excess provisioning and higher cost. This PR introduces smoothing to the burst allowance accrual, fixes an overcount in queued-request attribution, and expands per-pool utilization metrics to provide SLO-aligned observability.

review_comments: Asha Patel: Nice work. Please double-check the EMA alpha default; 0.2 felt aggressive in internal perf runs. Also a nit: rename metric dedicated_pool_utilization_p95 -> dedicated_pool_utilization_95p to match existing naming conventions.

release_notes:
- Introduced smoothed burst credit accrual to reduce transient scale-ups and improve cost stability.
- Fixed queued-request attribution bug that could trigger unnecessary scale events.
- Added per-pool utilization and burst credit metrics for better SLO-aligned observability (dedicated_pool_utilization_95p, burst_credits, burst_credit_accrual_rate).
- Feature gated: ENABLE_SMOOTHED_BURST_ACCRUAL (default off) to allow phased rollout.
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: enable gate off by default. Canary: enable for 10% of fleets for 48 hours and monitor dedicated_pool_utilization_95p and burst_credits. Watch for reduction in scale events and check tokenbucket_burst_usage. If any regression, toggle gate off. Migration: none required for stored state; metrics names changed (old metrics remain for 30 days).
impact_summary: This change reduces noisy scale-ups during short bursts, which lowers transient provisioning cost and improves stability for Dedicated customers. Observability improvements give SREs per-pool latency/utilization signals to tie to SLA alerts.
testing_performed: Unit tests for burst smoothing and queue attribution. Integration tests exercising autoscaler under synthetic burst traces (short spikes, sustained load, pool-switching). Load-tested on staging fleets with 100k qps synthetic traffic profile; observed 40% reduction in scale-up events for transient bursts and no negative impact on tail latency. Telemetry validated via metrics regression harness.
